question: Should production crawl-remote deployments permanently retain this hidden D1 canary and require predecessor-runtime canary support as a rollback precondition?
rationale: The choice intentionally couples persistent hosted data, production deployment success, rollback eligibility, and release ordering across repositories; tests can verify mechanics but cannot choose that operating policy.

options.title: Adopt With Staged Proof
options.body: Approve the permanent contract after the prerequisite PRs land and a staged deployment plus predecessor rollback succeeds against the reviewed releases.

options.title: Use Disposable Proof
options.body: Redesign validation around isolated or disposable data to avoid permanent D1 state and predecessor-runtime coupling.

options.title: Defer Production Enforcement
options.body: Retain the six-query evidence work but postpone the deployment gate until release operations are prepared to own the cross-release contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt With Staged Proof
recommendation.body: Approve the permanent contract after the prerequisite PRs land and a staged deployment plus predecessor rollback succeeds against the reviewed releases.

likelyOwner.reason: The available stack and commit history make this repository member the clearest owner of the full Gitcrawl deployment contract.
